title: Unit 3 · Places and weather
description: Countries, cities, geographic location, hay and estar, population, and basic weather.
source: Original exercises aligned to the Aula Internacional Plus 1 Unit 3 syllabus; no textbook exercise text copied.

cards.translation: Spain is in Europe.
cards.note: Use estar for the location of a country.

cards.translation: Mexico is in North America.
cards.note: Both América del Norte and Norteamérica are common.

cards.translation: Argentina is in South America.
cards.note: América del Sur means South America.

cards.translation: The capital of Spain is Madrid.
cards.note: Use ser to identify a capital.

cards.translation: The capital of Argentina is Buenos Aires.
cards.note: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina.

cards.translation: The capital of Chile is Santiago.
cards.note: Santiago is also called Santiago de Chile.

cards.translation: Portuguese is spoken in Brazil.
cards.note: Portugués carries an accent on the final syllable.

cards.translation: Spanish is spoken in Colombia.
cards.note: Español and castellano are both accepted here.

cards.translation: There is a museum in my city.
cards.note: Use hay to say that something exists.

cards.translation: There are many beaches in this region.
cards.note: Hay does not change for singular or plural nouns.

cards.translation: The museum is downtown.
cards.note: Use estar for the location of a known place.

cards.translation: The islands are in the Caribbean.
cards.note: Están agrees with the plural subject las islas.

cards.translation: Where is the station?
cards.note: Use estar when asking where a specific place is.

cards.translation: Is there a bank nearby?
cards.note: ¿Hay...? asks whether something exists.

cards.translation: There is no airport in the town.
cards.note: Put no directly before hay.

cards.translation: Madrid is a large city.
cards.note: Use ser for a general characteristic.

cards.translation: It is a very quiet town.
cards.note: Tranquilo agrees with the masculine noun pueblo.

cards.translation: It is a modern city.
cards.note: Moderna agrees with the feminine noun ciudad.

cards.translation: Barcelona is very touristy.
cards.note: Turística agrees with the feminine noun ciudad understood here.

cards.prompt: La ciudad ___ dos millones de habitantes.
cards.translation: The city has two million inhabitants.
cards.note: Spanish commonly uses tener to state population.

cards.translation: It has one hundred thousand inhabitants.
cards.note: Habitante has the same form for men and women.

cards.prompt: Tiene ___ de un millón de habitantes.
cards.translation: It has more than one million inhabitants.
cards.note: Más de means more than before a number.

cards.translation: It has fewer than fifty thousand inhabitants.
cards.note: Menos de means fewer than before a number.

cards.translation: How many inhabitants does the city have?
cards.note: Cuántos agrees with the plural noun habitantes.

cards.translation: What is the weather like?
cards.note: ¿Qué tiempo hace? is the standard weather question.

cards.translation: The weather is good today.
cards.note: Use hacer in many basic weather expressions.

cards.translation: The weather is bad today.
cards.note: Mal tiempo means bad weather.

cards.translation: It is very hot in summer.
cards.note: Spanish says hace calor, literally it makes heat.

cards.translation: It is cold in winter.
cards.note: Spanish says hace frío.

cards.translation: It is very windy on the coast.
cards.note: Hace viento means it is windy.

cards.translation: It is sunny today.
cards.note: Hace sol means it is sunny.

cards.translation: It is raining today. Take an umbrella.
cards.note: Llueve is the third-person singular of llover.

cards.translation: It is snowing in the mountains.
cards.note: Nieva is the third-person singular of nevar.

cards.translation: It is cloudy. We cannot see the sun.
cards.note: Use estar with nublado for a temporary condition.

cards.translation: The sky is clear.
cards.note: Despejado means clear or cloudless.

cards.translation: Spring comes after winter.
cards.note: La primavera is spring.

cards.translation: July is a summer month in Spain.
cards.note: El verano is summer.

cards.translation: Leaves fall in autumn.
cards.note: El otoño is autumn.

cards.translation: January is a winter month in Spain.
cards.note: El invierno is winter.

cards.translation: France is north of Spain.
cards.note: Al norte de means north of.

cards.prompt: El mar Mediterráneo está al ___ de España.
cards.translation: The Mediterranean Sea is east of Spain.
cards.note: Al este de means east of.

cards.translation: Mallorca is an island.
cards.note: Una isla is an island.
